Others have used the phrase: Equality before the law--that means equality before the laws which the well-to-do have made for the poor, and men for women. Others have maintained that the ideal of justice would be an inequality before the law adjusted to the differences between individuals.

9838-strong-hearts.title: Strong Hearts
9838-strong-hearts.creator: George W. Cable
9838-strong-hearts.description: A book by George W. Cable. h men, with countless lights, shades, narrownesses and breadths of meaning, call Religion, and taking it in the largest sense we can give it; in like manner taking Poetry in the largest sense possible; this cluster of tales is one, because from each of its parts, with no argument but the souls and fates they tell of, it illustrates the indivisible twinship of Poetry and Religion; a oneness of office and of culmination, which, as they reach their highest plane, merges them into identity.

arxiv-1510-03170.title: Fair and Square: Cake-Cutting in Two Dimensions Journal: Journal of Mathematical Economics
arxiv-1510-03170.creator: Erel Segal-Halevi, Shmuel Nitzan, Avinatan Hassidim and Yonatan Aumann
arxiv-1510-03170.description: Abstract We consider the classic problem of fairly dividing a heterogeneous good ("cake") among several agents with different valuations. Classic cake-cutting procedures either allocate each agent a collection of disconnected pieces, or assume that the cake is a one-dimensional interval. In practice, however, the two-dimensional shape of the allotted pieces is important.

arxiv-1808-03543.title: Introducing fully UP-semigroups This work was financially supported by the University of Phayao.
arxiv-1808-03543.creator: Aiyared Iampan
arxiv-1808-03543.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce some new classes of algebras related to UP-algebras and semigroups, called a left UP-semigroup, a right UP-semigroup, a fully UP-semigroup, a left-left UP-semigroup, a right-left UP-semigroup, a left-right UP-semigroup, a right-right UP-semigroup, a fully-left UP-semigroup, a fully-right UP-semigroup, a left-fully UP-semigroup, a right-fully UP-semigroup, a fully-fully UP-semigroup, and find their examples.

arxiv-2305-16977.creator: F. Argentieri, B. Fayad
arxiv-2305-16977.description: Abstract We prove rotations-reducibility for close to constant quasi-periodic S ​ L ​ ( 2 , ℝ ) SL(2,{R}) cocycles in one frequency in the finite regularity and smooth cases, and derive some applications to quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators. Introduction In this paper we will study smooth quasi-periodic SL(2,{R}) cocycles in one frequency.

arxiv-2309-10856.title: Non-equilibrium critical scaling and universality in a quantum simulator
arxiv-2309-10856.creator: A. De, P. Cook, K. Collins, W. Morong, D. Paz, P. Titum, G. Pagano, A. V. Gorshkov, M. Maghrebi, C. Monroe
arxiv-2309-10856.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A. De, P. Cook, K. Collins, W. Morong, D. Paz, P. Titum, G. Pagano, A. V. Gorshkov, M. Maghrebi, C. Monroe. Universality and scaling laws are hallmarks of equilibrium phase transitions and critical phenomena 1 ; 2 ; 3 . However, extending these concepts to non-equilibrium systems is an outstanding challenge. Despite recent progress in the study of dynamical phases 4 ; 5 , the universality classes and scaling laws for non-equilibrium phenomena are far less understood than those in equilibrium 6 .

arxiv-2407-13355.title: EarlyMalDetect: A Novel Approach for Early Windows Malware Detection Based on Sequences of API Calls
arxiv-2407-13355.creator: Pascal Maniriho, Abdun Naser Mahmood, and Mohammad Jabed Morshed Chowdhury
arxiv-2407-13355.description: Abstract In this work, we propose EarlyMalDetect, a novel approach for early Windows malware detection based on sequences of API calls. Our approach leverages generative transformer models and attention-guided deep recurrent neural networks to accurately identify and detect patterns of malicious behaviors in the early stage of malware execution.

arxiv-2411-19468.title: Learning Expressive Random Feature Models via Parametrized Activations
arxiv-2411-19468.creator: Zailin Ma, Jiansheng Yang, Yaodong Yang
arxiv-2411-19468.description: Abstract The random feature (RF) method is a powerful kernel approximation technique, but it typically uses fixed activation functions, limiting its adaptability across diverse tasks. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Random Feature Model with Learnable Activation Functions (RFLAF), a novel statistical model that parameterizes activation functions as weighted sums of basis functions within the random feature framework.

arxiv-2412-21125.title: Optimal e-value testing for properly constrained hypotheses
arxiv-2412-21125.creator: Eugenio Clerico
arxiv-2412-21125.description: Abstract Hypothesis testing via e-variables can be framed as a sequential betting game, where a player each round picks an e-variable. A good player’s strategy results in an effective statistical test that rejects the null hypothesis as soon as sufficient evidence arises.

arxiv-2507-06095.title: Traveling waves in a continuum model of schooling swimmers Preprint: Preprint #
arxiv-2507-06095.creator: Anand U. Oza, Eva Kanso, Michael J. Shelley
arxiv-2507-06095.description: Abstract The complex formations exhibited by schooling fish have long been the object of fascination for biologists and physicists. However, the physical and sensory mechanisms leading to organized collective behavior remain elusive. On the physical side in particular, it is unknown how the flows generated by individual fish influence the collective patterns that emerge in large schools.

arxiv-2510-25896.title: Atmospheric collapse and re-inflation through impacts for terrestrial planets around M dwarfs
arxiv-2510-25896.creator: Prune C. August, Robin Wordsworth, Mikayla Huffman, David Brain, Lars A. Buchhave
arxiv-2510-25896.description: Abstract Detection of an atmosphere around a terrestrial exoplanet will be a major milestone in the field, but our observational capacities are biased towards to tidally locked, close-in planets orbiting M-dwarf stars. The atmospheres of these planets are vulnerable to atmospheric erosion and collapse due to condensation of volatiles on the nightside.

arxiv-2512-24347.title: The period map from commutative to noncommutative deformations
arxiv-2512-24347.creator: Samuel A. Moore

arxiv-2601-19968.title: What is the AGI in Offensive Security?
arxiv-2601-19968.creator: Youngwoong Cho
arxiv-2601-19968.description: Abstract What is the AGI in Offensive Security? One can break it down into two questions : (1) any offensive security tasks could be reduced into symbolic language manipulation (language representation + reasoning), (2) powerful language model (LLM) are enough to "deal with" any symbolic language manipulation.

arxiv-2601-21365.title: Small models, big threats: Characterizing safety challenges from low-compute AI models
arxiv-2601-21365.creator: Prateek Puri
arxiv-2601-21365.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are revolutionizing fields such as medicine, drug discovery, and materials science; however, many technologists and policymakers are also concerned about the technology’s risks. To date, most concrete policies around AI governance have focused on managing AI risk by considering the amount of compute required to operate or build a given AI system.

Due to the small number of patients, it is difficult to stratify all patients of CS by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) analysis.

pmc-11496053.title: Neural effects of multisensory dance training in Parkinson’s disease: evidence from a longitudinal neuroimaging single case study
pmc-11496053.creator: Jenny R. Simon, Judith Bek, Katayoun Ghanai, Karolina A. Bearss, Rebecca E. Barnstaple, Rachel J. Bar, Joseph F. X. DeSouza
pmc-11496053.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Dance is associated with beneficial outcomes in motor and non-motor domains in Parkinson’s disease (PD) and regular participation may help delay symptom progression in mild PD. However, little is known about the neurobiological mechanisms of dance interventions for PD. The present case study explored potential neuroplastic changes in a 69-year-old male with mild PD participating in regular dance classes over 29 weeks.

pmc-11516458.title: Advancing Public Health Equity through Expanded Vaccination Services in prison: case studies from Italy and France
pmc-11516458.creator: N Cocco, R Ranieri, M Polidoro, E Murauer, A Meauset, F Meroueh
pmc-11516458.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In Montpellier prison in France and San Vittore remand house in Italy, the provision of expanded, age-appropriate, coercion-free, and tailored vaccination services to PLP has emerged as a cornerstone in improving health outcomes within prison settings. The implementation of life course vaccination programs required the full integration of prison health into public health systems building on existing vaccination services covering HBV, flu and COVID-19. In San Vittore, a vaccination clinic aimed at people living in prison was set-up.

pmc-11545818.title: Fava Bean Protein Nanofibrils Modulate Cell Membrane Interfaces for Biomolecular Interactions as Unveiled by Atomic Force Microscopy
pmc-11545818.creator: Sanjai Karanth, Marina Wiesenfarth, Julia Benthin, Melanie Koehler, Jiajia Song, Emanuele Zannini
pmc-11545818.description: Functional amyloids (protein nanofibrils, PNF) synthesized from plant sources exhibit unique physicochemical and nanomechanical properties that could improve food texture. While environmental factors affecting PNFs are well-known, scientific evidence on how cells (focus on the oral cavity) respond to them under physiological conditions is lacking.

pmc-11862199.title: Guanfacine in the Treatment of a Child Diagnosed with Tourette Syndrome: A Case Report
pmc-11862199.creator: L. T. Durán Sandoval, M. D. C. Blasco Fresco, E. de la Fuente Ruiz
pmc-11862199.description: Introduction Tourette syndrome (TS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by the development of persistent and changing motor and phonic tics over time. The presence of at least two motor tics and one vocal tic that have persisted for at least a period of 1 year is required, and which developed before the age of 18.

pmc-12579858.title: Outpatient Process Transformation and Patient Satisfaction Under New Public Service Theory
pmc-12579858.creator: Zejun Cai, Ali Wu, Xiaofeng Wang, Haofen Xie
pmc-12579858.description: ObjectiveTo explore the impact of outpatient process transformation guided by new public service (NPS) theory on patient satisfaction.MethodsA total of 600 outpatients were randomly selected for satisfaction surveys before and after the process transformation, which was designed and implemented based on the principles of NPS theory. The transformation targeted areas with satisfaction scores below 9 points.

pmc-12705666.title: Single copy optogenetic system for Streptomyces
pmc-12705666.creator: Airi Watanabe, Ryuta Noya, Rio Yamada, Hideaki Takano
pmc-12705666.description: LitR is a blue-green light-sensing transcriptional regulator that uses coenzyme B12 as a chromophore. In this study, we developed a genome-integrative light-inducible expression (iLiEX) system in Streptomyces griseus NBRC 13350, a Gram-positive bacterium that produces streptomycin. The system incorporates LitR, transcriptional amplification module T7 RNA polymerase, and a serine integrase.

pmc-13183506.title: Identification of a genetic locus responsible for the dominant white-spotting coat phenotype in mice spontaneously isolated from a Japanese wild-derived inbred strain
pmc-13183506.creator: Hiromitsu OCHIAI, Gou TAKAHASHI, Yuki ISHIDA, Yoshibumi MATSUSHIMA, Kenta WADA
pmc-13183506.description: Agouti-dominant spotting (Ads) is a novel mutant mouse that was spontaneously isolated from KOR1/Stm (KOR1), an inbred strain derived from a Japanese wild mouse. Heterozygous Ads mice exhibit dominant white-spotting on the dorsal coat, whereas homozygous mice display embryonic lethality. We generated [Ads×C57BL/6J (B6)]F1 (F1), F2 and [B6×(Ads×B6)]N2 (N2) mice to investigate the inheritance patterns of the Ads phenotype.

pmc-13584947.title: Chemotherapy-Induced Remodeling of the Gut Microbiota–Inflammation Axis: Implications for the Course of Bipolar Disorder
pmc-13584947.creator: Sinuo Li, Siqi Wang, Yuxuan Ren, Jun Yan
pmc-13584947.description: There is growing evidence that bipolar disorder, BD and cancer share several biological features, including immune dysregulation, gut microbiota alterations, and chronic inflammation. Chemotherapy remains a mainstay of cancer treatment but can substantially alter the gut microbial ecosystem, impair intestinal barrier integrity, and contribute to systemic inflammation.

pmc-13609754.title: Research Progress on Acidizing Techniques for Complex-Type Reservoirs
pmc-13609754.creator: Yujie Bai, Yifei Sun, Chao Xu, Mingxing Bai, Jiashu Wu, Jingfang Cui, Guangsheng Cao, Gen Li
pmc-13609754.description: With the continuous decline in easily recoverable reserves of conventional oil and gas, the focus of oil and gas exploration and development has gradually shifted toward complex reservoirs, such as low-permeability, tight, high-temperature and high-pressure (HTHP), and strongly heterogeneous reservoirs. Such reservoirs are characterized by complex pore–throat structures, poor seepage capacity, extreme temperature and pressure conditions, and strong heterogeneity.

pmc-13670417.title: Effect of Dietary Papaya (Carica papaya) Leaf Meal on Growth Performance and Haematological Responses of Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) Fingerlings Reared in a Recirculating Aquaculture System
pmc-13670417.creator: Farhabun Binte Farhad, Farzana Yasmin Ritu, Moupia Mustafi, Md. Abdus Salam, Shaharior Hashem
pmc-13670417.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In the pursuit of sustainable aquaculture, the integration of unconventional plant‐based feed additives like papaya leaf meal (PLM) offers a promising approach for enhancing fish growth while reducing feed costs and environmental impact. To evaluate the efficacy of PLM as a growth promoter, four experimental diets were formulated by gradually incorporating PLM at inclusion levels of 0%, 3%, 6% and 9%.
